newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends flat in moderate trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends flat in moderate trading.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar finished flat at C$1.3440 (US$0.7440) on Tuesday from C$1.3443 (US$0.7439) on Monday after a moderate session, traders said.
* The currency strengthened overnight on overseas buying, but retreated in morning trade on Tuesday after bouncing off the key C$1.3410 (US$0.7457) level.
Despite losing much of its strength today, the market is generally positive on the Canadian dollar, traders said.
Financial markets are awaiting the outcome of a two-day meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee which ends on Wednesday.
Economists said the Bank of Canada is unlikely to match any increase in U.S. rates in the coming months as long as the Canadian dollar maintains its recent strength.
Canada's central bank confirmed on Tuesday that the economic fundamentals which pushed short-term Canadian rates to their lowest point in decades remained intact.
In its winter review, the central bank said that the output gap, the room that the economy has to grow before sparking inflation pressures, would narrow but not disappear in 1997.

"With the amount of excess supply in the economy remaining large, the trend of inflation is expected to stay in the lower part of the inflation-control target range of one to three percent in coming months," the bank said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar climbed to 1.2252 marks from 1.2197 marks on Monday and rose to 90.99 yen from 90.51 yen on Monday.
